chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon both of them) who said:
I asked him about a woman whose husband dies while she is still in her waiting period (iddah); does she receive maintenance (nafaqah)? He said, 'Maintenance is not spent on her from her own wealth.'

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: A woman whose husband has died

ai.seo_question: Does a wife receive maintenance from her own wealth during the waiting period after her husband's death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies that a widow’s maintenance during her *iddah* is drawn from the deceased husband’s estate rather than her own personal wealth, distinguishing it from the *iddah* of divorce. This ruling underscores the financial protection afforded to widows under Shia jurisprudence, ensuring their sustenance is a right against the estate before inheritance distribution. The hadith highlights the practical application of Quranic provisions regarding widows' rights and maintenance.
